title.narrative: Greater Mekong Subregion Capacity Building for Human Immunodeficiency Virus Infection/Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome (HIV/AIDS) Prevention Project

description.narrative:
The project impact is to contribute to achieving and sustaining the Millennium Development Goal to have halted and begun to reverse the spread of HIV/AIDS in the Lao PDR and Viet Nam. The expected outcome of the project will be increased coverage and quality of services for targeted populations in 23 border provinces. The project has four outputs.
Output 1: Strengthened planning and management capacity at national, provincial, and district levels. Output 2: Enhanced capacity to provide quality and accessible services to people vulnerable to HIV transmission. Output 3: Improved access to HIV prevention outreach among target populations in communities and cross-border areas. Output 4: Effective and sustainable regional collaboration to strengthen HIV response established.

description.narrative: Increased coverage and quality of services for targeted populations

80% of targeted populations (including FSWs and ethnic women) reached by the project can articulate correct information on HIV transmission and means of prevention by 2018 Progress/Status: Lao PDR: The PMU is processing the recruitment of the consulting firm to conduct baseline survey. The survey will include capacity to articulate correct information on HIV transmission and means of prevention. IBBS conducted by CHAS in 2011 among service women in 6 provinces found that “95% knew that condom protects against transmission of HIV in vaginal sex, but only 85% knew that condom protects against transmission of HIV in anal sex. Altogether, 84% of the service women knew that condom protects against transmission of HIV while having sex” “93% of service women knew that HIV is transmitted from mother to child during pregnancy or delivery” “90% of service women knew that HIV is transmitted through sharing contaminated needles (90%).” “Misconceptions on HIV modes of transmission have decreased substantially compared to the previous round of surveillance as 65% know that mosquitoes are not vectors for HIV transmission; 81% know that a healthy looking person can be infected with HIV; and 84% know that HIV is not transmitted through sharing a meal with a person living with HIV. Moreover 71% knew that there are some medications that can extend the life of people living with HIV. One third of the service women still believe that taking antibiotics before having sex prevents from getting infected with HIV and more than half of the service women working in Vientiane Capital believe the same.” “The global AIDS reporting progress (GARP) indicator measures the proportion of respondents who knows that: condom protects against sexual transmission of HIV (anal and vaginal), faithfulness is a coping strategy against HIV transmission, PLHIV can look healthy, sharing food with PLHIV is not risky, and mosquitoes are not vectors for HIV. The GARP indicator was at 32% overall. However there were some differences between provinces with Vientiane capital at the lowest end (19%). In Luang Prabang, 60% of the service women provided correct answers to the GARP indicator, which contrasts with the low level of condom use reported in this province. The GARP indicator was not associated with any of the measures of condom use.”
The PMU is processing the recruitment of the consulting firm to conduct baseline survey. The survey will include capacity to articulate correct information on HIV transmission and means of prevention.
VIE: The endline survey conducted in Jan 2018 revealed that 86% of IDU, 68% of EM, and 76% of MMP can articulate correct information on HIV transmission and means of prevention , slightly increased from the first survey carried out in Nov 2016. Data Source: Baseline and endline surveys Baseline value: 0.0

Use of HIV/AIDS services (VCT, ART) and community prevention services among targeted groups increased by 50%, and by 30% for PMTCT (disaggregated by sex) in targeted provinces by 2018 (Viet Nam) Progress/Status: Compared to baseline in 2013. • Number of HIV tests conducted increased by 74% from 112,663 in 2013 to 195,612 in 2017, in which increase for women and pregnant women were 50% and 36%, respectively. • Number of AIDS patients under ART increased by 78% from 9,636 in 2013 to 17,130 in 2017. • PMTCT: Number of HIV positive pregnant women who received ART increased by 85% from 128 in 2013 to 237 in 2017. • Number of new MMT patients increased by 90% from 1,587 in 2013 to 3,010 in 2017. Female patients under MMT increased from 1 in 2013 to 54 in 2017. • From 2014 to 2017, an average of 46% of ethnic villages received at least one BCC session, representing over 100% increase as compared to 21% of ethnic villages received at least one BCC session in 2014. Data Source: Routine monitoring reports at health facilities Baseline value: 0.0

Use of HIV/AIDS services (VCT, PMTCT, ART) and community prevention services among targeted groups increased by 50% (disaggregated by sex) in targeted provinces by 2018 (Lao PDR) Progress/Status: CHAS M&E unit collects monthly data on HIV-AIDS services from all service sites. The data is disaggregated by sex. For VCT, it includes number of users, number of tests conducted, number of positive tests, number of users who got the result of the test, etc. Data is disaggregated and provides the same information for PMTCT. Data on ART services are also available from CHAS M&E system. The regular existing reporting system does not allow to get results by ethnicity yet. However, the patient record computerized monitoring evaluation recording system (MERS) that collects data from each patient will allow disaggregating by ethnicity. The project is supporting the roll out of the MERS through various activities including procurement of computers, training, supervision. 2014 data for 8 target provinces: -VCT: 15,716 (12060 females) -PMTCT: 7526 -ART: 530 2015 data for 8 target provinces: -VCT: 23,259 (17,247 females) -PMTCT: 13,163 -ART: 687 (338 females) Data regarding community prevention services among targeted groups are collected through the project data collection system developed by CHAS and PCCAs. Data Source: Routine monitoring reports at health facilities Baseline value: 0.0

Output: Effective and sustainable regional collaboration to strengthen HIV response established Indicator: Cross-border collaborative gender sensitive activities for migrant and mobile populations piloted in 3 sites by 2014 Progress/Status: O4: Pilot was planned in 2014/2015 for 4 paired provinces in Vietnam (Thanh Hoa, Kom Tom, Dien Bien, Binh Phuoc), and 3 in Laos. The pilot activities included communication campaign, mass media communication at community (radio), and training in BCC.
In 2016, the implementation was expanded to total 7 provinces in Vietnam (Dien Bien, Son La, Thanh Hoa, Kon Tum, Ha Tinh, Quang Nam, and Quang Tri). c
By December 2016, following activities were implemented: - Communication training for commune/village leaders: 2,230 people [women: 876 (39.3%) and minority: 1,446 (64.8%)]. - BCC sessions: 302 sessions; estimated 30,567 people attended with of about 24,546 minority people (80.3%); 1,910 mass media communication via loudspeakers. - Harm reduction: + Received needles: 2,324 people [4 women (0.2%), 1,695 EM (72.9%)]. + Received condoms: 2,884 people [34 women (1.18%), 1,952 EM (67.7%)] - Number of people counselled and tested: 1,265 [women: 688 (54.4%) and 251 (19.8%)].
Data Source: Project implementation reports Baseline year: 2012 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2012 Baseline value: N Target year: 2018 Target value: Y

To date, number of target population reached by mobile clinics increases from 1,978 in 2015 to 3,055 (2,002 or 65% are female) in 2016, and 3,659 (2,614 or 71% are female) in 2017 (as of June 2017). Output: Strengthened planning and management capacity at national, provincial, and district levels Indicator: Gender-sensitive HIV plans are fully integrated into provincial AOPs in Viet Nam by 2018 Progress/Status: O1: In March 2017, VAAC issues guidelines for development of annual provincial HIV/ AIDS prevention and control plan which include gender-sensitive HIV strategy (i.e. prevention and care for pregnant women). All provinces are required to comply with the strategies stipulated in the guidelines. Data Source: Provincial AOPs in Viet Nam Baseline year: 2012 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2012 Baseline value: N Target year: 2018 Target value: Y

Output: Strengthened planning and management capacity at national, provincial, and district levels Indicator: Gender-sensitive HIV plans are fully integrated into provincial AOPs in the Lao PDR by 2018 Progress/Status: O1: Annual operation plans prepared by the provincial health offices follow MOH's standard planning template. HIV prevention and care interventions are systematically integrated into the plans.
With regard to gender sensitivity, AOPs for FY 2014/2015 have been reviewed by the international and national gender consultants recruited in May 2015.
During the workshop in April 2015 on review of progress of the project implementation and preparation of the project AOPs for the year 2015-2016, CHAS presented to PCCAs from the 8 target provinces the project gender and ethnic group action plan and provided recommendations on integration of project activities in the plan. The national BCC and gender consultants recruited in May 2015 prepared specific integrated activities in the AOPs for FY 2015-2016. This includes mainstreaming gender and ethnic group sensitivity into plans, dissemination of GEGAP and DMF indicators to monitor, review of training and BCC materials, TOTs, conduct awareness activities on HIV/AIDS prevention using gender mainstreaming and ethnic sensitized materials with BCC in target villages. Data Source: Provincial AOPs in the Lao PDR Baseline year: 2012 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2012 Baseline value: N Target year: 2018 Target value: Y

Output: Strengthened planning and management capacity at national, provincial, and district levels Indicator: Routine sex-disaggregated monitoring data are used for annual work plan in all target provinces and districts in the Lao PDR Progress/Status: O1: Sex-disaggregated data collection is integrated into the project's monitoring and evaluation system.
CHAS completed training on project management and planning for PCCAs and DCCAs. It also conducted trainings on mapping of target populations and rapid assessment of high risk behaviors. This data is used by DCCAs and PCCAs to prepare annual operational plans with activities directed to these high risk groups. PMU and CHAS requested in June 2015 PCCAs to provide an update of the high risk populations targeted in each province. The update is provided in Appendix 8 of the quarterly report. High risk populations targeted in each province was updated during the first quarter of 2016. The update in provided in appendix 9 of QR 10. The target population mapped in 2016, subject to revision if necessary, will be the basis for preparation of AOP 2017.
